content.title: Chapter 102 - UTILITIES — Sec. 102-76. - Maintenance of service lines.

faqs.a:
The maintenance and protection of privately owned piping, including service line and
               fittings, pressure reducing valves, meter pits, fixtures and water-using appliances,
               except meters whether located in or upon public or private property, are the sole
               responsibility of the user, except as otherwise set forth below. The city is not responsible
               or liable for damage from any cause whatsoever to such piping, fixtures, appurtenances
               and water-using appliances, and no user is entitled to reimbursement for damages or
               payment of refunds by reason of pressure changes or stoppage of the flow of water
               through the system. The protection of water-using devices and systems which require
               limited or sustained water pressure or a continual water supply is the responsibility
               of the user who will provide suitable protective devices, including pressure reducing
               valves for such apparatus at the owner's expense. The city will make available the
               following service to permitted premises:
(1)
Repair of leaks on user service lines, which have curb stops, will be performed by
                  the department of utilities on that segment of the user's service line which lies
                  between the water main and the outlet side of the curb stop. The user will repair
                  all leaks that emanate from the threads on the outlet side of the curb stop and all
                  other service line appurtenances on the outlet side of the curb stop.
(2)
Repair of leaks on user service lines that have outdoor meters and no curb stop will
                  be performed by the department of utilities on that segment of the service line which
                  lies between the water main through and including the valve at the inlet side of the
                  meter and the meter-attaching coupling. The user will repair all leaks emanating from
                  the service line or any of its appurtenances located on the outlet side of the meter
                  yoke. The user will maintain the meter pit.
(3)
Repair of leaks on user service lines that do not have curb stops or outdoor meters
                  will be performed by the department of utilities only on that portion of the service
                  line that is outside the user's property boundary or within a recorded easement for
                  the service line. The user will repair all leaks emanating from the service line or
                  any of its appurtenances located inside his property line.
(4)
Repair of leaks on user service lines which are connected to privately owned fire
                  lines will be performed by the department of utilities as set forth above, as applicable,
                  except that any repair will include repairs on that segment of the fire line between
                  the main and the outlet side of the isolation valve on the fire line, or the property
                  line, whichever is closer to the city water main. The department of utilities assumes
                  no responsibility for maintenance or repair of fire lines which are free of domestic
                  service lines except those with isolation valves located in city rights-of-way or
                  at the user's property line, in which case the department of utilities will maintain
                  that segment of the fire line that lies between the city water main and the outlet
                  side of the isolation valve. However, if a user does not promptly repair a leak, the
                  city may make any necessary repairs at the expense of the user or the owner. The city
                  may recover the actual cost of the work or expense as provided in
section 102-41
.
(5)
The user is responsible for all damage to persons or property resulting from leaks
                  from the service line or appurtenances thereto.
(6)
Where a single connection but a common service line serves more than one user independently
                  metered and further where the common service may branch and cross both properties,
                  develops a leak between the meters and the city water main, whether the service line
                  is in an easement or private property, all of the users served through the single
                  connection are jointly and severally responsible for all costs to repair the leaking
                  service line. The city has the right to repair the leak after notification to the
                  user and then to bill the repair costs and cost of unmetered water lost equally to
                  all users.
(7)
Any maintenance provided by the department of utilities under this section will not
                  include any responsibility for either the thawing of frozen service lines or appurtenances
                  or repairs to stub-in connections.
(8)
The repair and servicing of meters will be as provided for in
section 102-61
.
(9)
The repair service as hereinabove described will be provided without cost to the user
                  only for those leaks that are attributed to normal wear and aging of the service pipe.
                  Leaks caused by actions such as excavation, demolition, or the department of utilities
                  will not repair landscaping upon the customer's property and repair of such leaks
                  is the responsibility of the user. The unmetered water lost due to the broken service
                  line will be billed to the user at the lost water rate as set forth in
section 102-179
. The estimated volume of lost water will be estimated based on service line size,
                  break size, water pressure, and flow time.
(10)
Should the city perform any work or incur any expense for the installation, removal,
                  replacement, servicing, relocation, or maintenance of a water service line or appurtenances
                  thereto, and any such work or expense is the responsibility by either the user or
                  the owner, the city is authorized to recover the actual cost of such work or expense
                  as provided in
section 102-41
.
(Code 1981, § 33-47; Ord. No. 2574, § 1, 11-21-1988; Ord. No. 2671, §§ 8—11, 10-16-1989;
               Ord. No. 2823, §§ 6—8, 7-1-1991)
